title: Iran Central Bank Governor Says Economy Won't Collapse Under U.S. Pressure; Vows to Turn U.S. Economic War Back on U.S.
text:
Iran Central Bank Governor Says Economy Won't Collapse Under U.S. Pressure; Vows to Turn U.S. Economic War Back on U.S."

"🔆🔅TEHRAN - October 7 - Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor, late last night, October 6th, made some remarks during a televised interview."

""
"SOT1, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "I have a message for the U.S. Treasury Secretary and other U.S. officials: only five days remain in the two-week deadline they [the United States] gave, saying that the country’s [Iran's] economy was going to collapse. And here we are, discussing the country’s economic achievements, and I am telling them that this will not happen.""

"SOT2, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "The U.S. government is a ruthless government. You can see how they martyred our children in [the southern Iranian city of] Minab, how they martyred our beloved Leader, and many others [during the war]. They [the Americans] were supposed to bring Iran to the point of collapse within two weeks [as a result of the war], achieve victory, and leave. They have now been at it for nine months. Then, 10 days ago, they announced that they wanted Iran to collapse economically within two weeks. Ten days have now passed since that announcement. And now, at the front line of the economic war, we will give them the same response, meaning that they will get the same result [and face economic collapse].""

"SOT3, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "Now, in the economic war, just as they [the Americans] kept saying [during the military war] that 90 percent of their [Iranians'] missiles had been used up and so on, only to see more and more missiles raining down on them, the same thing is happening now [in the case of the economic war]. They keep saying that Iran’s foreign exchange reserves are running out, its revenues are drying up, and then they see that nothing has happened [to Iran]. Ultimately, they apply psychological pressure, engage in propaganda, and put pressure on the governments of regional countries. They are using all these measures to apply pressure and, in any case, break the Iranian economy. I assure the people that the Iranian economy will not be broken by these measures.""

"SOT4, Abdolnaser Hemmati, Iran's Central Bank Governor: "From the beginning of the year until roughly the middle of [the month of] Mehr [on the Iranian calendar (corresponding to October 7)], we have provided $24.9 billion in foreign currency. That is a significant amount; we have provided nearly $25 billion in foreign currency for the country, meaning that goods worth that amount have been imported into the country. The $25 billion compares with $28 billion during the same period last year, that is, from the beginning of last year up to this date. So, [in comparison] we have [only] had a 12-percent decrease in the provision of foreign currency.
